Hem!

oh! (surprise, glad or not)

(vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.; also Cic. (Rab. Post. 45))

Lewis & Short: surprise in a good or a bad sense, admiration, joy, grief, indignation. The commonest “oh!” of comedy; the manuscripts often confuse it with em (“there!”, see here you are).

Other words

  • Ehem! — oh! (glad surprise, on meeting someone)

    also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 901: Ehem, pater mī, tū hīc erās?; Plaut. Asin. 449b: Ehem, optume. quam dūdum tū advēnistī?; Traupman 327

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

    Lewis & Short: “an exclamation of joyful surprise”. The word for “oh, it’s you!”.

  • Oh! — oh! (any strong feeling)

    also used · classical · Plaut. Cas. 522b: Oh, nimium scītē scītus es.

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

    Lewis & Short: “for the most various emotions”: surprise, pleasure, sorrow, aversion; repeated, oh oh oh, in lament (Plaut. Capt. 200a).

  • Ō …! — oh (with a name, or exclaiming at something)

    with the vocative, or the accusative of exclamation · also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 790: Ō caelum, ō terra, ō maria Neptūnī!; Cic. Att. 13.52.1: ō hospitem mihi tam gravem!

    Not a word on its own: it opens an address or an exclamation.

Examples

  • Hem, Dēmea, haud aspexeram tē. Quid agitur?

    Oh, Demea, I hadn’t seen you. How are things?Ter. Ad. 373–374

  • Quid agitur, Aeschine? — Ehem, pater mī, tū hīc erās?

    How are you, Aeschinus? — Oh, Dad, you were here?Ter. Ad. 901

  • Quis hīc loquitur? ehem, tūne hīc erās, mī Phaedria?

    Who’s that talking? Oh, was it you here, my Phaedria?Ter. Eun. 86

  • Oh, nimium scītē scītus es.

    Oh, you’re far too clever by half.Plaut. Cas. 522b

  • Ō caelum, ō terra, ō maria Neptūnī!

    O heaven, O earth, O seas of Neptune! (mock-tragic: good for a dropped cup)Ter. Ad. 790

See also ah!, wow!, oh no!, oh dear!, here you are.
